slides.say: The operation diamond is defined for every positive number x. It is known that for every positive x, diamond of diamond of x is equal to x. Which of the following can be the definition of the operation diamond?
No definition, just a property. Do the diamond twice, and you're back at x. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, plugging in numbers, and then by understanding.
[short pause] Let's put each rule on trial. Pick a test value, not zero, not one. Two. Six x, two goes to twelve, and twelve goes to seventy-two. Not two, out. x plus six, eight, then fourteen. Out.
x over six, one third, then one eighteenth. Out. Six over x, two goes to three, and three goes back to two. Choice number four is our answer.
at: Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way. What's different? We know which families undo themselves, c minus x and c over x. Ten minus, ten minus x, is x again. And six over, six over x, is x again.

So six over x, choice number four. Watch choice number three, x over six. It looks close, but the x is on top, and it just keeps shrinking. And a step property, like one step up in the input gives three times the result? Test two neighbours, like two and three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
